name: Introducing the IPRAM Lab for Tokenized Regulated Asset Markets
description:
The tokenisation of regulated real-world assets has led to multiple institutional implementations of the same financial instruments, each operating on its own infrastructure with few shared patterns for how those infrastructures interoperate. As a result, tokenised assets remain confined to the environment they were issued in, accessible only to counterparties already inside the same institutional perimeter.

The IPRAM Lab ([https://github.com/LFDT-IPRAM](https://github.com/LFDT-IPRAM)) develops open implementation patterns for the interoperation of tokenised real-world regulated financial assets and the markets they participate in. This session introduces the lab's mission, scope, and the initial interoperability challenges it aims to address. All interested parties are invited to join!

**ZOOM LINK TO JOIN:** **[https://zoom.us/my/hyperledger.community.3?pwd=UE90WHhEaHRqOGEyMkV3cldKa2d2dz09](https://zoom.us/my/hyperledger.community.3?pwd=UE90WHhEaHRqOGEyMkV3cldKa2d2dz09)**

name: Designing for the Robot: A content persona for the AI era
description:
Large language models, AI assistants, and search engines are rapidly becoming some of our most important content consumers. But most content strategies are still designed with only human audiences in mind. In this session, Jackie Pysarchuk introduces the concept of the robot persona—a practical framework for designing content that serves both people and AI systems. Expanding on ideas from her forthcoming article on the Button blog, attendees will explore how content structure, metadata, governance, and lifecycle management influence AI visibility and answer quality, and leave with practical ideas they can apply to make their content more discoverable, understandable, and useful in an AI-driven world.

**About Jackie**
Jackie Pysarchuk is Senior Director, Web Content and Strategy at the American Bankers Association and a content strategist specializing in enterprise web strategy, governance, and AI-ready content. Throughout her career, she has helped organizations including the American College of Cardiology, Northrop Grumman, and Yes& build scalable content systems that improve both user experience and business outcomes. Jackie writes and speaks about the future of content strategy, with a focus on designing content for AI, search, and emerging digital experiences. Her latest work introduces the concept of the "robot persona," encouraging content teams to treat AI systems as a first-class audience alongside humans.

The Washington Area Unity Users Group (WAUUG) is back.

We’re restarting the group with a casual meetup for Unity developers, game developers, artists, students, hobbyists, industry professionals, and anyone interested in building interactive experiences.

You do **not** need to be a Unity expert. Beginners, students, experienced developers, indie creators, professional teams, and people who are simply curious about game development are all welcome.

If you have something you're building, bring it. If you have something you want to learn, bring questions. If you've been looking for other developers and creators in the area, come meet them.

name: How to build an agent-ready IDP with open source tools
description:
A portal is just a front door. The real complexity of an Internal Developer Platform (IDP) sits in the backend layer beneath it. As autonomous AI agents begin using your platform, traditional setups built only for human developers face immediate security gaps and operational bottlenecks. Join Sameera Jayasoma and Lakmal Warusawithana, maintainers of the CNCF OSS project OpenChoreo, as they show how to build an agent-ready platform without a multi-year custom build.

In this session, you will learn:
- **Platform vs. portal:** Why a portal alone is not enough, and how owning the backend execution layer speeds up software delivery.
- **Designing for AI agents:** How to give AI agents their own identities, limited access, and safety rules when interacting with your APIs, shifting your engineering team from working _inside_ the loop to _orchestrating_ it.
- **Practical open source adoption:** How to use a modular architecture like OpenChoreo to connect the Kubernetes, CI/CD, and monitoring tools you already run, turning your existing tools into secure, agent-ready golden paths
